LIS (LedelsesInformationsSystem) is a regional management information system in Denmark utilized for local data validation and clinical quality assurance. It plays a critical operational role in the workflow of the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB), which is a national quality database tracking acute high-risk abdominal surgery. Data regarding patient populations and clinical indicators from the AKDB has been available within the regional LIS environments since September 2020 [^src1]. 

The primary function of LIS in this context is to enable hospitals and regions to validate their local clinical registrations against national records. Medical and administrative staff use the system to compare data from their local electronic patient records (EPJ) with data reported to the National Patient Register (LPR) and subsequently forwarded to the AKDB via KKA deliveries [^src1]. This rigorous comparison ensures that the reported patient population accurately reflects actual clinical reality. The validation process relies on highly precise variable definitions—such as 'Opereret = 1' and 'T_0'—as well as hospital-level identifiers like 'Forloeb_SORKode' [^src1]. 

By facilitating this direct, localized data comparison, LIS acts as a practical trigger for continuous quality improvement work across Danish regions and hospitals. It is fundamentally tied to the broader quality development strategy overseen by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), bridging the gap between national database reporting and local clinical practice [^src1].
